title: The Craving Brain
coreMove: Find the reward the cue starts promising before the routine begins.
sourcePressure: Claude Hopkins and Pepsodent anchor the chapter's narrower claim: a cue becomes powerful when the reward is expected in advance. Anticipation makes a loop sticky, which is why some new routines catch while others stay as reminders.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version repeats cue, routine, reward or turns the chapter into advertising trivia. The writer must isolate craving as the pull of an anticipated payoff, not as a slogan for motivation.

hook: A generic product-marketing opener about clever ads.
A person deciding to become motivated overnight.
A toothbrush or toothpaste scene that simply retells Pepsodent.
counterintuition: Most people think reminders create habits, but actually cravings do.
Treating craving as dopamine shorthand with no visible expected reward.
Making the chapter another cue-routine-reward recap.
tryThisNow: Set a timer for ninety seconds and imagine a reward.
Make the habit fun with no specific expected payoff.
Add a generic reminder to a routine and call it craving.

exampleSpecs.domain: apartment-building compost pilot in a high-rise with contamination fines
exampleSpecs.audience: a resident-council organizer whose reminder signs have failed
exampleSpecs.stakes: the building will lose its compost service if residents keep dropping food scraps into the wrong chute
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast the ignored rules poster with the new chute-room board showing a clean bin and rent-credit tally; the resident sees the tally, smiles before opening the caddy, and the cue now promises the clean-room reward before the sorting starts.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A banana peel hovers over a green countertop caddy.

exampleSpecs.domain: youth orchestra scale practice with a private recording reward
exampleSpecs.audience: a violin teacher whose eleven-year-old student only practices songs, never scales
exampleSpecs.stakes: the student will keep missing auditions if the dull preparation never feels connected to the sound she wants
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The teacher tapes a QR sticker inside the violin case that plays last week's clean four bars; when the student opens the case and hears the sound, she reaches for the bow before being reminded because the cue has made the reward arrive early.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rosin dust freckles the velvet inside a violin case.

exampleSpecs.domain: climbing gym warm-up wall before first lead route
exampleSpecs.audience: a climbing coach trying to make beginners warm up without nagging
exampleSpecs.stakes: cold shoulders and skipped warm-ups are producing preventable injuries on busy evenings
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The coach asks whether a reminder sign will change anything, then adds a small bell climbers can ring only after the warm-up circuit; by Friday they touch the easy rungs while looking at the bell because the cue now carries the expected send-day payoff.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A chalked hand pauses under the easiest rung on the warm-up wall.
mustAvoid: random reward unrelated to the routine

exampleSpecs.domain: public library manga checkout challenge for reluctant teen readers
exampleSpecs.audience: a teen services librarian whose overdue warnings are not bringing books back
exampleSpecs.stakes: a grant-funded reading program will fail if returns feel like punishment instead of a path to the next volume
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The librarian slides the next-volume cover into a clear pocket beside the return slot; the teen sees the cover before dropping off the old book and asks for the sequel, showing the cue has begun promising the next-story reward.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A glossy manga cover peeks from a clear pocket beside the return slot.

exampleSpecs.audience: a festival coordinator whose volunteers keep arriving late for second shifts
exampleSpecs.stakes: empty door posts could delay screenings and strand ticket holders outside in the rain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The coordinator can send another scolding email, but instead pins each lanyard under a Polaroid of the full theater the volunteer helped open; the volunteer reaches for the lanyard because the cue previews the applause and full-house reward.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A red volunteer lanyard hangs below a Polaroid of a packed theater.

exampleSpecs.domain: freelance wedding photographer file-backup ritual after receptions
exampleSpecs.audience: a photographer who knows backups matter but still postpones them after late events
exampleSpecs.stakes: one corrupted memory card could erase a client's only record of the night
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: After a near loss, she places a printed thank-you note beside the drive dock; when she sees it at 1:12 a.m., the relief of safe delivery arrives before the copy begins, and the backup cue finally pulls the routine forward.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A silver memory-card wallet sits beside a printed thank-you note.

skillTargets: identify the anticipated reward that makes a cue pull before the routine starts
distinguish a bare reminder from a cue that carries an expected payoff
choose habit designs where the payoff is made near, specific, and felt in advance
analyze why a new routine failed when the reward stayed abstract or delayed

tryThisNowSpec: Put one cue for a wanted routine beside a tiny preview of its payoff: a finished line, saved photo, checked card, or first sound. Notice whether the preview makes you reach sooner.
